question: In February _____, Mahatma Gandhi decided to withdraw the non-cooperation movement.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1922.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Non Cooperation Movement:**

 
 
• **In 1920**, during British rule, **Gandhiji started the first national movement known as the Non-Cooperation Movement (NCM).**
 
• There were several factors that contributed to the Non-Cooperation Movement. The main causes include the **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre, the Rowlatt Act,** and** the Khilafat Movement**.
 
• In **September 1920**, during a **special session held in Calcutta**, the **Congress supported** a Non-Cooperation Movement until the injustices of Punjab and Khilafat were rectified and Swaraj was achieved.
 
• **The Nagpur INC Session of December 1920** saw the **acceptance and endorsement** of the non-cooperation programme without any resistance.
 
• The campaign was characterized by the boycott of foreign products, government services and legal practice, legislative bodies, courts, and government-run institutions and colleges.
